falha-silenciosa.d: Numerical damage that raises no error or exception: the model stays fluent but starts getting more things wrong (arithmetic, needles, tool calls). It is the typical failure mode of quantization and of bad kernels, which is why it calls for measuring instruments.

teacher-forcing.d: Evaluating the model by feeding it a whole real text and reading, at each position, the next-token distribution, without letting the model follow its own choices. It does not depend on sampling and costs a single prefill, but it is not bit-deterministic (the numerics still vary between runs); it is the basis of NLL, KLD and top-1 agreement.

surpresa.d: \( -\ln p \): how unexpected the token that came was, according to the model. Zero if \(p=1\), large if \(p\) is small. Measured in nats (ln) or bits (log₂).

nats.d: Unit of information based on the natural logarithm (1 nat ≈ 1.443 bits). The recipes report KLD and NLL in nats per position (or per token).

nll.d: Mean of \( -\ln p_\theta(x_t\mid x_{<t}) \) over the positions of a text: the average surprisal on the true tokens. It is exactly the cross-entropy loss used in training.

perplexidade.d: \( e^{\text{NLL}} \): the effective number of options the model seems to be hesitating between. Only comparable with the same text and the same tokenizer, and it hides errors that cancel out in the mean.

entropia-cruzada.d: \( H(P,Q) = -\sum_v P(v)\ln Q(v) \): the average surprisal of using \(Q\) to predict what \(P\) generates. It equals \( H(P) + D_{KL}(P\|Q) \).

kld.d: \( D_{KL}(P\|Q)=\sum_v P(v)\ln\frac{P(v)}{Q(v)} \): how far the candidate’s next-token distribution \(Q\) strays from the reference \(P\), in nats, averaged over positions in teacher forcing. Always ≥ 0 and asymmetric; far more sensitive than perplexity.

prompt-logprobs.d: vLLM parameter (on /v1/completions, with echo) that returns, for each position of the prompt itself, the log-probabilities of the top-\(k\) tokens and that of the observed token. It is what makes it possible to measure NLL and KLD through the API.

kl-top-k.t: KL on the top-k support (KL proxy)
kl-top-k.d: KL computed only on the tokens present in the top-\(k\) lists of both sides, renormalized. It ignores the tail: it typically underestimates the true KL when the top-\(k\) covers almost all of the mass, and can be off in either direction when it does not. Useful for comparing arms measured in exactly the same way.

top-1-agreement.d: Fraction of positions where the candidate’s most likely token matches the reference’s. Intuitive (it is what greedy decoding sees), but unstable on near-ties.

margem-top2.d: \( \ln p_{(1)} - \ln p_{(2)} \): the distance, in nats, between the most likely token and the runner-up. Small margins are near-ties that swap places with numerical noise.

flip-de-argmax.d: A change of the most likely token at a position between two runs or two arms. On near-ties, it happens even between identical stock runs.

painel-calibrado.d: A numerical screen that first measures the stock’s own variation (≥ 4 captures) and only then judges the candidate against it, on the stable positions only: consensus flips, separation, and KL standardized by each position’s null (2× gate). Outputs: WITHIN (0), FLAG (1), UNQUALIFIED (2). It only counts as a gate if the stock control passes it.

nulo-stock.d: The distribution of the differences between repeated runs of the system with no change at all. It is the ruler a candidate is judged against; a candidate “within the null” is indistinguishable from noise.

not-worse.d: Non-inferiority verdict of the formal studies (in GLM, the kl_panel from llm-quality-suite): the candidate’s NLL change stays within the tolerance derived from the stock, \(\max(\text{stock range},\ 0.005)\) nats/token.

equiv.d: Equivalence verdict, stronger than NOT-WORSE: the candidate fits within the band occupied by the stock pairs themselves. It often comes out inconclusive, because the stock barely fits in its own band.

inconclusivo.d: An outcome in which the instrument cannot judge, for example because the control (the stock treated as a candidate) failed a gate. It is neither a pass nor a fail.

controle-positivo.d: A candidate known to be bad, included in the study to prove that the instrument detects damage (in GLM, the W8A8 path: 7.99× the null and 23 flips). The negative control is stock against stock.

protocolo-congelado.d: Protocol and thresholds fixed, with a published hash, before the first measurement, so that nobody can choose the threshold after seeing the data.

regra-de-tres.d: If 0 events were observed in \(n\) trials, the 95% upper bound for the rate is ≈ \(3/n\), because \(-\ln 0.05\approx 3\).

rel-rmse.d: \( \lVert \hat W - W\rVert_F / \lVert W\rVert_F \): the fraction of the signal that became noise in quantization (or between two kernels). Per-channel FP8 E4M3 gives ~2.4–2.7% on real weights.

similaridade-cosseno.d: \( \langle \hat W, W\rangle / (\lVert\hat W\rVert\,\lVert W\rVert) \): alignment between the quantized tensor and the original. For a small, unbiased error, ≈ \(1 - \text{rel}^2/2\).

paridade-numerica.d: A test that compares the output of a candidate kernel or path with that of a reference, on the same inputs, with an explicit tolerance (fixed, or calibrated by stock-vs-stock noise).

oraculo-numerico.d: A slow, readable reference implementation (for example in NumPy) of a format or kernel, used as ground truth to test the optimized version.

quantizacao-simulada.d: Quantizing and immediately dequantizing, in high precision, to reproduce a format’s error without actually using it. Used in quantization-aware training (QAT) and in parity checks.

nao-associatividade.d: \((a+b)+c\) can differ from \(a+(b+c)\) because every addition rounds. Variable reduction orders (split-K, atomics, top-k, batch composition) change the last bits of the output.

determinismo-bit-a-bit.d: Identical runs produce outputs that are identical down to the last bit. It requires a fixed reduction order; temperature 0 and a fixed seed are not enough.

finalize-fundido.d: The step that sums, weighted by the router, the outputs of each token’s top-k experts, fused into the GEMM. In FlashInfer CUTLASS, the fused version may reduce in a variable order; the unfused one has a fixed order.

ruler.d: NVIDIA’s synthetic long-context benchmark (arXiv:2404.06654) that goes beyond the simple needle: needles with several keys, variable tracking (multiple hops) and aggregation (most common words).

variable-tracking.d: A RULER task: a chain VAR A = 12345, VAR B = VAR A, … in the context; the model must list every variable holding that value. It measures multi-hop reasoning, not just retrieval. In ruler-lite, there are 5 variables and 4 hops, interleaved across 20 sentences at the start of the prompt.

cwe.d: A RULER task: a numbered list in which a few words appear far more often than the others; the model must say which are the most frequent. It measures aggregation. In ruler-lite, 5 words ×10 and 45 ×3 (185 items), in a contiguous list at the start of the prompt.

garble.d: Degenerate output: an echo of the prompt, a dump of the tool schema, a leaked secret, special tokens, an answer starting in the middle of a word. In DeepSeek-V4, it showed up mostly in deep, cold prefill.

loop-degenerado.d: The model starts recycling sentences it has already emitted and never recovers. Raising max_tokens does not help; it is detected by a persistent drop in n-gram novelty.

cauda-longa.d: A healthy but long generation: the model keeps saying new things and simply ran out of budget. Raising max_tokens fixes it.

novidade-ngrama.d: The fraction of a window’s n-grams (here, 8 consecutive words) that never appeared earlier in the same trace. Healthy text stays high; a loop collapses to near zero.

bateria-de-ferramentas.d: A fixed set of tool-calling checks (simple, complex schema, parallel, multi-turn, forced, truncation) run against the server, with the JSON validated and the finish_reason checked.

gate-de-qualidade.d: An objective criterion that a change must pass before it becomes the default (e.g., RULER-lite 8/8, 145/145 cases, NOT-WORSE on kl_panel). It only counts if the control (the unchanged stock) passes it.

erro-padrao.d: The standard deviation of an estimate. For an accuracy rate \(\hat p\) over \(n\) questions, \(\sqrt{\hat p(1-\hat p)/n}\); differences smaller than 2 or 3 standard errors cannot be told apart from luck.

humaneval.d: OpenAI’s benchmark of 164 Python programming problems: the model writes the function from its signature and docstring, and unit tests decide whether it passes (pass@1). With so few problems, each one is worth ~0.6 percentage points.

teste-por-hash.d: A check that compares the hash of two replies’ tokens (in TensorFold, the token_sha) instead of measuring a distance. It only works on an exact engine, where the stock-vs-stock null is zero: it passes on equality the changes that preserve the bits and fails any different bit, but it cannot grade lossy changes.

gsm8k.d: A benchmark of grade-school math problems with verifiable numeric answers; the test set has 1,319 questions. Useful, but coarse-grained near the ceiling.

fronteira-de-pareto.d: The set of non-dominated options: no other option is at least as good on every axis (e.g., bytes and KLD) and strictly better on one. Choosing outside it is waste.

recibo-de-medicao.d: A raw, dated record of a measurement (JSON, logs, hashes of the inputs, image and .env version), kept so that someone else can redo or audit the conclusion.
